author: MonkeySlap
body:
Application
Age: 14
Timezone:
Do you have access to TeamSpeak? Yes/No: 
Do you have access to Skype? Yes/No: 
Do you have access to a recording software? Yes/No: 

CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?

Well, I am currently the NetworkOwner on MedievalCraft (medievalcraft.myserver.gs)
I was Administrator on WavePvP (wavepvp.myserver.gs) Went down due to funding
I was Helper on SharkPvP (sharkpvp.myserver.gs) I resigned due to idiotic Owners
I was Owner on SharpPvP (sharp.myserver.gs) Went down due to funding
I had an application on LitPvP (litpvp.com) that was accepted, but for some reason I didn't go to the interview.

What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?

My "Biggest Weakness" would maybe be that I am not that familiar with the protocol of Avicus. This, of course means that I am not sure which punishments fit which offense. This can be easily fixed, as I'm sure you will make staff members highly familiar with the protocol while they are serving.

My "Biggest Strength" would most likely be that I am an amazingly fast typer. I am a natural multitasker, and I am able to tackle many problems at once. Meaning, if a player Private Messages me with a question, people are spamming the reports about a pesky hacker, a ban evader joins, and two more players are spamming me with questions. All in all, this is five "Problems" for me to deal with. How my mind works, is that I tackle the first problem immediately. Whether it's typing '/ban IanPlayzMC Ban Evasion' or typing '/r You can apply for Moderator on the Forums', I will be able to type it quickly. Then I quickly tackle the remaining four problems. One after another. Combining this amazing multitasking skill with my lightning fast fingers, I'm the dream staff member.


How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
Well, for one, I will do my best to rid Avicus of hackers. Those pesky players come right on and ruin the game for others. Seeing as hacking is bannable, it shouldn't be too hard to '/ban' them as soon as I see they are hacking. Another way I can help improve the staff team, is I can ease the workload of other staff members. I understand that staff members get flooded with requests, reports and questions. I can definitely help with that. I am totally able to help out other staff members by easing their workload. A final way I can help improve the team, is that I can add a touch of humor to the server. Believe me, nobody wants to play on a server that acts too cordial and too robotic. My name: MonkeySlap, and my skin are both examples of how I can add a touch of humor to Avicus. Don't get me wrong. I will still be professional. Nobody wants to talk to a 100% mature person.


What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
A leader needs to be able to work with others. Meaning, others may have other perks and needs that some might find exhausting and annoying. A leader would have to push through, still work with them. Act professional and cordial, even though the person annoys them to death. Another quality people need to see in a leader is just that: Leadership. A leader needs to take the reins. To steer him and his allies to victory! A leader needs to rise up and take charge! I do, in fact consider myself to be a leader. For one, I participate in an international club called Destination Imagination. This club works on leadership skills, teamwork skills, etc etc etc... In my opinion, I excel at it. I am natural leader. I hold the ability to keep order, and Ma'at (peace) among everyone. I wish to use this ability as a staff member on Avicus.

What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
Well, I'd have to list an example as my "Biggest Strength" for an attribute. I am an extremely fast typer. Faster, than most, and I have a unique multitasking ability that allows me to get many things done quickly, and to the best of my ability. Another example is my natural leadership skills. I would be able to keep the peace accordingly, and punish wrongdoers accordingly. An obvious, and probably much heard attribute, is that I am really just a nice person. I am more-or-less non-toxic and I know my way around the forums.

What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?
Well, of course, you would need the skill of being able to listen. Some people are extraordinarily slow typers, and you must still listen to them. My last example gave me the idea of my next skill: Patience. Whether it's waiting for a player to reply, or waiting for a hacker to show his hacks so I can '/ban' him, I think I have patience to beat the band. A third skill needed to interact with the community is the "Skill of Knowledge". As I mentioned before, I am not too up-to =-date with the current protocols needed for Offense -> Punishment, but I am sure I can be caught up in that field. I have much experience playing on Avicus. I have been playing since the server was named WallsMC, and the ip was WallsMC.Net. Those were the days. A final skill needed to interact with the Avicus community is the skill of asking for help. If I would be accepted, I assume I would be granted a trial rank. A trial rank wouldn't have much power, so I would need to ask for help or submit a staff report to get someone banned.

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 
A rough idea of committed time would be AT LEAST Seven Hours a week. So that's an hour a day. That's the absolute minimum. I will be playing A LOT on weekends, and at least an hour per school day. Call that a "Rough Idea"



CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?

The "Correct Answer" to this kind of depends on protocol, so I will be giving a solution according to a guessed protocol by me. If a Trial position has access to '/ban', I would continue to gain evidence and '/ban' according to protocol. If the hacking evader continues to join, I would continue to mock him and /ban him according to protocol. If this carries on for over half an hour, I would get a higher staff member to ip ban him. If a Trial position does not have access to '/ban', I would gather evidence and contact a '/ban' worthy staff member. If this hacker evader continues to evade, then I would contact a higher staff to ip ban him. If there are no online '/ban' worthy staff members to contact, then there's really nothing I'd be able to do. I suppose I'd just be able to collect evidence of him hacking/evading, and wait it out while convincing him to leave. That's really all I'd be able to do.


Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?
Honestly, I have access to TeamSpeak, but I'm not that educated in its inner workings. I'm really not sure how much power someone has by being referee, but I'll take a good crack at this one: I'd join the leaders in asking him to leave, and if he refuses, I'd tell other people to leave his channel, as long as it's not bad for the server. I honestly have no idea.


A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realize that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?
Hmm... This is a good question. Let me start out by saying, I have a nice anti corruption software on all of my files, so this wouldn't be able to happen to me. However, I would push that the player would still be punished, and I would check to see if any other staff members had gathered evidence. If not, and the player got off, I would watch him/her like a hawk and try and catch him at it again.

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
Let me see if I understand the question: The staff member shows a screenshot of a thread to the public. However, the public isn't supposed to see the screenshot. Only staff members are. In this case, I'd immediately report the staff member to higher authority for disclosing sensitive or private information.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?
You know what? I respect the Senior Staff Team enough to vote with them. However, if I am expressedly interested in this specific decision, I'd try as hard as I can to learn more about it, then speak my mind on my opinion. Any good leader is a good listener, and respect my decision, or at least factor it into a final decision. Not to criticize the Senior Staff, of course. This is just a question about personal values, and I'm all 'bout the values!

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?
Well, firstly and obviously, it would mean that I would be in a position of respect. I would, of course, not abuse this position, but respect it and use it for the good of Avicus. I think a staff position on Avicus would mean a lot to me. I've been playing for quite a bit, and I think that it would mean a lot to me if I were given a higher position. Higher, even, than the Gold rank. Just on a personal level.

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?
I am extremely passionate about Avicus. Avicus stands for me originality, cleverness, efficiency, and of course, entertainment. I've been having fun on Avicus for years now. Avicus means to me, a good time. A good time playing Minecraft. For example, a little while back, I was tempbanned for excessive caps. I immediately felt terrible and joined on with an alt, then that alt got banned for ban evasion, etc, etc, etc... In the end, the whole thing was wiped from my records, so please don't take this into consideration when you are deciding if I would be a good addition to the staff team.

Do you speak any other languages than English?
I am conversational in Latin and Dutch. Not much else. Sorry.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?
I really hope that you guys choose me. I really do. I am one of your oldest customers on Avicus, and hopefully soon I will be staff. All together, I am a fast typer, multitasker, and I am getting into plugin design soon. I hope to be the future of Avicus. I can't wait to start!


Good luck to those applying
- Senior Staff.
